# Harness The Power of “Global Webhook” In SurveySparrow

Global Webhook — One Webhook For All Surveys

## What is a webhook?

Webhook is a method for one system to notify another system about events or updates.

For instance, let’s take **application A** and **application B**. If you want to inform application B every time a specific event happens in application A, that’s where webhook comes in.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*Yif6VCDobtoubiHJ)

Difference between repeated **API calls** and **Webhooks**

Now, let’s explore the **outgoing webhook** feature implemented in SurveySparrow.

In SurveySparrow, webhooks are embedded into a workflow such that they streamline the process of transferring data between applications. This is particularly useful for non-developers to automate workflows.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*RkbWtd-HzKjWFWkna6GoVg.png)

Webhook in SurveySparrow’s Workflows

A perfect example would be integrating Discord with survey responses. So, if you want to notify your team through Discord every time you receive a new response on a specific survey, you can do so via webhooks.

But, in the above example, the webhook is strictly restricted such that it can be implemented for each survey separately since it is situated in the **integrate** tab of a survey.

But, what if the same webhook functionality could be applied to all surveys at once?

That’s where the Global Webhook comes in.

## Global Webhook

It allows users to set up an application, where they just need to specify the **Endpoint URL of the third-party application** andselect the events. So, every time those events get triggered in SurveySparrow, the event payload will be sent to this endpoint URL.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:1000/1*SUz1CLtXJ0RyCZy6dfxwMQ.png)

Automating Data transfer from SurveySparrow to Discord through Global Webhook

Let’s dive deep into how to create a webhook app in SurveySparrow.

## Pre-requisites

As a developer, the global webhook might be required when you want to fetch the information when specific events happen in your SurveySparrow account. Hence, it is required to have a server and an endpoint URL to which the event payloads will be sent.

## Step 1:

Let’s locate the webhook in your SurveySparrow account

- In your SurveySparrow account, go to **settings** -\> **Apps and Integrations**(located in the left menu panel) -> click on **Developer Portal**
- You will find two tabs — **APPS and WEBHOOK** -\> Click on **WEBHOOK**

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*petNQ45067C9iXy4)

## Step 2:

It’s time to create a webhook app!!

Click on **\+ New Webhook** and fill in all the necessary details. The detailed information of what each field represents is defined below.

- **App Name** — As the name suggests, you can provide an appropriate name that’s relevant to the functionality you want to implement.
- **Short Description** — Here, it’s highly useful to provide the necessary information, the purpose of this webhook app, unobvious configurations, and other important details.
- **Support Email** — This is crucial to specify because if the webhook you created malfunctions or if the endpoint URL throws errors for 24 hours, you will be notified via this email.
- **Support URL (Optional)** — Provide a support URL through which SurveySparrow’s support team can contact you regarding any issues with your webhook app.
- **Website Link (Optional)** — Provide a website URL that you are associated with such as your company’s website, personal website, etc. This is to verify the identity of the user who’s creating the webhook app.
- **App Icon (Optional)** — Upload a suitable app icon that’s minimalistic and relevant.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*YVmXttjSdrMKW7hK)

## Step 3:

This is the crucial step in creating the webhook app. There are important configurations here that determine the security of the webhook.

### **Secret Token**

The secret token helps in the process of verifying that the event payload is sent from SurveySparrow to your server.

### **Endpoint URL**

Enter a valid URL to which the event payload should be sent via a POST request. Click on the **validate** button to verify that the URL is valid.

### **Authentication Header (Optional)**

This is where you can specify extra headers to the POST request and there is an option to keep it default as well. These extra headers provide added security to your webhook.

To understand in-depth about the implementation of the authentication headers, refer to this [**documentation**](https://sdk.surveysparrow.dev/docs/global-webhook/#configurations).

**Basic Authentication**

This is one type of Authentication where it requires a **username** and **password** to be sent with the headers.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*lzCPd5TLwUwoSLVi)

**OAuth Authentication**

If your application needs OAuth authentication, specify the **client ID**, **client secret**, **token URL, and Scope(Optional)** of your app.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*KGbmV_FiSsWe8SIa)

**Token Authentication**

Token Authentication is quite similar to OAuth Authentication but here you can only specify **client ID**, **client secret**, and **token URL**.

The **scope** is not defined in token Authentication.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*kBFxPkvEpHhRb4Fe)

In both Token Authentication and OAuth Authentication, the platform expects the token URL to return the response in the below format.

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "access_token":"MTQ0NjJkZmQ5OTM2NDE1ZTZjNGZmZjI3",
  "token_type":"Bearer/Basic",
  "expires_in":3600,
}
```

**Custom Headers**

As the name suggests, it allows you to specify customized key-value pairs which you can send as part of the headers.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*nXI7aLn-1Wi2RJlf)

## Step 4

This is the exciting part.

Here, you can select the events whose data you want to fetch. Below are the commonly used events in SurveySparrow.

- **onSubmissionComplete** — When a user submits a response to any survey
- **onContactCreate** — When a new contact is created
- **onContactUpdate** — When a new contact is updated
- **onContactDelete** — When a new contact is deleted

Check out this [link](https://sdk.surveysparrow.dev/docs/serverless/#sample-payloads-of-each-of-the-events) to find the list of all the other events.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*ubD2UOBVfbaSMQgq)

For instance, let’s say you’ve selected the **onSubmissionComplete** event. Now, every time a response is submitted in any of the surveys in your SurveySparrow account, a POST request is made to the endpoint URL with the event payload in the body of the request.

The same applies to all of the events mentioned above. You can select multiple events on one webhook app as well.

Click **Save** and your webhook is created successfully!!

After creating the webhook, you can find it in the developer portal under the webhook section.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*h9ICSmIRwuD16eUH)

## Key Considerations

1. Rate limiting is enforced on Global Webhooks. It restricts each event payload transmission to a **maximum of 5000 occurrences per day for a single webhook**. In simple terms, 5 **000 payload transmissions/event/day/webhook**
2. In the body of the POST request sent to the endpoint URL, the data will be sent in a format similar to the one given below. The event payload varies for each event.
